scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, indicating roughly a doubling since August.
Route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a shortfall in manual meter reads that could lead to estimation errors and contribute to the dispute surge.
The observation shows dispute ticket response times are well within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3 days SLA), indicating that response speed is not a driver of the dispute surge.
The observation shows that disputed bills are higher for actual reads (1785) than for estimated reads (1240), indicating that the dispute surge is not primarily driven by estimation errors.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff alterations were logged during the period.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing delayed routes and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder asserts that no tariff changes occurred this year, indicating tariff alterations are not a factor in the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but require Field Operations Manager confirmation, indicating that such changes are subject to human approval per the dispatch policy.
